title: Do Agentic Contexts Inflate Evaluation-Awareness Enough to Break Agentic Safety Evals?

original_idea.body:
# Do Agentic Contexts Inflate Evaluation-Awareness Enough to Break Agentic Safety Evals?

**Problem:** Tool-use/file-exploration contexts amplify evaluation-awareness, but this is not connected to the agentic safety evaluations governance relies on for autonomy thresholds.

**Direction:** Build matched bare-prompt vs agentic-environment task suites of the same safety probes, measure awareness/behavior divergence on open models, quantify resulting bias in agentic safety eval scores.

**Why it matters:** Capability-threshold governance leans on agentic evals; if those are most awareness-contaminated, thresholds are mis-calibrated.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2603.03824 (March 2026).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: agentic-eval bias directly affects capability-threshold calibration, a recognized critical governance pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Build matched task suites + measure divergence on open models; guided though agentic setup adds friction.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused matched-suite comparison with a clear bias metric; some setup dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: External open-model study of agentic-eval contamination labs underweight; neglected.

low_compute.reasoning: Agentic runs on open models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The in-context-awareness result exists; connecting it to agentic governance evals is the open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The base result exists; the agentic-governance-eval connection is the open extension.
